script: My husband vanished, eviction papers arrived—what I did next shocked us both.. I got eviction papers on Tuesday. My husband had been dodging the lot rent for months, and now the paper said we'd be out of our trailer if we didn't pay. I am the one paying the daycare, phones, half the power, mortgage, and internet. He's the one paying his car and the lot rent. We kept everything in separate accounts, thought we were good. Then the landlord hit us with that notice. I called the VP of regional management at the park. She's helping us set up a payment plan and putting the eviction on hold. Thank God, but this isn't the first time we've hit a financial snag—our car got repoed before. Now the house might get taken. I sat down with him, no daughter in the room—she was at grandma's. I said, "I love you, but I love our daughter more. If you can't be financially responsible, you won't be financially responsible for her. I will be. You'll still see her, she'll still have a dad, but I'll be the primary." It wasn't a conversation I wanted to have, but it had to happen. I am giving him a last chance, but I am also questioning whether I can keep this marriage going. I am the one juggling all the bills, and I am exhausted. I am setting up an account to monitor his money—both our checks go in, and I am the one managing everything. I don't want to weaponize his finances, but I feel like I have no other choice. I am at a loss.
